item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 112330
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Fri Sep 11 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Norbert, located well west-southwest of the southern tip of
the Baja California Peninsula.

Central and Western East Pacific (EP97):
Showers and thunderstorms continue to become better organized in
association with a broad area of low pressure located several
hundred miles southwest of the southwestern coast of Mexico. Gradual
development of this system is likely, and a tropical depression is
expected to form during the next day or two while it moves generally
west-northwestward to westward over the central and western portions
of the eastern Pacific basin.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...70 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Well Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
A broad trough of low pressure located several hundred miles
southeast of the Hawaiian Islands is producing disorganized showers
and thunderstorms. Gradual development of this system is possible
during the next few days while it moves generally northward and then
meanders.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...20 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Kelly

item.description:

WTPZ34 KNHC 120249

BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Norbert Advisory Number  10
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
500 PM HST Fri Sep 11 2026
 
...NORBERT HOLDING STEADY ON A WEST-NORTHWEST TRACK...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 PM HST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.2N 126.6W
ABOUT 1150 MI...1855 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
ABOUT 1870 MI...3015 KM E OF HILO HAWAII
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...65 MPH...100 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 285 DEGREES AT 12 MPH...19 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...996 MB...29.42 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM HST (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Norbert was 
located near latitude 17.2 North, longitude 126.6 West. Norbert is 
moving toward the west-northwest near 12 mph (19 km/h), and this 
general motion is expected to continue over the next couple of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 65 mph (100 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Gradual strengthening is forecast over the weekend, and 
Norbert is forecast to become a hurricane on Saturday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 105 miles (165 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 996 mb (29.42 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Pierce/Gibbs

item.title: Tropical Storm Norbert Forecast Discussion Number 10
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Fri Sep 11 2026 
241 
WTPZ44 KNHC 120250
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Storm Norbert Discussion Number  10
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
500 PM HST Fri Sep 11 2026

Satellite imagery indicates that the convective organization 
associated with Norbert has changed little over the past several 
hours. A well-defined curved band of deep convection continues to 
wrap into the circulation around the western semicircle from the 
north, although cloud-top temperatures within the band have warmed 
slightly during the past few hours. The latest subjective Dvorak 
intensity estimate from TAFB maintains T3.5/55 kt, which harmonizes 
well with the objective intensity estimates from UW-CIMSS ranging 
between 45 and 55 kt. Given these data and only modest changes in 
the convective structure, the initial intensity is held at 55 kt.

The initial motion is west-northwestward, or 285/10 kt. This general 
westward to west-northwestward motion is expected to persist through 
the weekend as a low- to mid-level subtropical ridge remains 
positioned north of the cyclone. Thereafter, confidence on Norbert's 
general motion is reduced as track models diverge significantly, as 
the evolution of the mid-level ridge plays a vital role in the track 
forecast over the next several days. The GFS shows the ridge 
shifting eastward, causing Norbert to generally prevail westward, 
while remaining on the north side of the guidance envelope. On the 
other hand, the ECMWF showcases the aforementioned ridge building 
southward, steering Norbert more southwestward. The consensus aids 
sit snug in between these two solutions. The NHC track forecast 
sides largely with the previous forecast, which lies near the Google 
DeepMind ensemble mean. 

Environmental conditions appear favorable for some strengthening, 
and Norbert is forecast to become a hurricane within the next 24 h. 
Thereafter, Norbert's intensity is expected to remain relatively 
consistent, shuffling 5 to 10 kt difference throughout the forecast 
period. This will depend ultimately on the track, as discussed 
above. A more northward track, more in line with the GFS, would find 
Norbert in a less favorable environment, where increasing vertical 
shear would weaken the system considerably. Conversely, the more 
southern track similar to the ECMWF, would bring Norbert into a more 
favorable environment with less vertical wind shear, allowing 
Norbert to potentially strengthen. Given the competing scenarios 
thereafter, little change has been made to the previous intensity 
forecast, with some weakening still indicated early next week. The 
NHC intensity forecast is generally an update to the previous 
advisory.
